Daniel — appreciate the packet. I've completed a line-by-line response and included examples and configuration notes in the attached PDF. Highlights and clarifications below (pulling from the attached Redwood_IAM_Response_2028.pdf):

SSO (SAML / OIDC)
- Protocols: SAML 2.0 (AuthNRequest, SP metadata available) and OIDC (Auth Code + PKCE).
- Initiation: Both IdP-initiated and SP-initiated supported. Recommend SP-initiated for redirect reliability; IdP-initiated supported for IdP-driven workflows.
- Logout: SP-initiated SLO supported for SAML; OIDC logout endpoint available. Session termination is best-effort across browsers — we document recommended IdP settings in the PDF.
- Attribute mapping: SAML NameID and OIDC sub/email claims are mappable to Redwood user attributes. Example SAML metadata attached (saml-metadata-redwood.xml).

SCIM provisioning & schema
- SCIM 2.0 endpoints support Users and Groups by default.
- PATCH semantics: support for RFC 7644 JSON Patch-style operations (add/replace/remove) as well as bulk PUT for full syncs. We accept both PATCH op-based and bulk provisioning patterns depending on customer preference.
- Rate limiting: per-tenant provisioning throttles are configurable; default is 200 req/min with burst capacity.
- Example SCIM schema and sample requests attached (scim-schema-sample.json).

RBAC & Admin Controls
- Role model: predefined roles (Org Admin, Security Admin, Billing Admin, Model Owner, Read-Only) and custom role creation.
- Delegation: Org Admins can grant subset roles scoped to projects or models. Cross-tenant delegation is supported via service principals + explicit grant flows (recommended for MSP-like scenarios).
- Session controls: configurable session idle/absolute timeouts, MFA enforcement on admin flows.

Audit & Retention
- Provisioning audit: every SCIM transaction is logged with request/response payloads (redacted for secrets) and operator identity; logs are retained 90 days by default and can be extended to 7 years on enterprise plans.
- Evidence: sample audit export and retention policy included in the PDF.

Attachments included: Redwood_IAM_Response_2028.pdf, saml-metadata-redwood.xml, scim-schema-sample.json

If you have specific callouts in the questionnaire that need text responses for the procurement packet, call them out and we will produce redlined text. We can also stand up a short sandbox for you to test SCIM workflows.

Thanks,

Hi Daniel — Neha from Redwood's Identity team. Answers below and samples attached.

1) PATCH semantics: our implementation prioritizes SCIM "Operations" (RFC 7644) with an "add/replace/remove" operations array. We also accept RFC 6902 JSON Patch when customers request it (we translate to our internal ops). Primary: RFC 7644 (operations array). Note: for large group deltas we recommend PATCH with a replace semantics or bulk PUT for efficiency.

2) Correlation IDs: every provisioning API call returns an X-Request-ID header and a provisioning_transaction_id in the JSON response. The audit export includes both values for correlation. Example: provisioning_transaction_id: "ptx-9f3b2e"; X-Request-ID: "req-2028-05-23-11-45-7b6a".

3) Delegated admin UX for cross-tenant service principals:
- Create service principal in customer tenant and exchange a short-lived onboarding token via our admin API
- Grant explicit project scope via our AdminRoles API (Org Admin or Security Admin must approve)
- Service principal inherits only the scoped permissions; any escalation requires an approval step captured in the audit log

Samples attached:
- scim-patch-example.txt (group membership add/remove sample)
- provisioning-audit-sample.csv (sanitized export, includes timestamps, operator_id, provisioning_transaction_id, request/response codes)

Operational notes:
- Rate limits: default 200 req/min per tenant; we can raise this for dedicated customers or add burst windows during initial provisioning.
- Error behavior: we follow standard 2xx/4xx/5xx semantics; transient 429s include Retry-After with suggested backoff.

I'll upload the sandbox tenant and a short README with curl examples if you'd like to test the flows; propose a Thursday 11:00 ET deep-dive if that works for your team.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Identity Engineer, Redwood Inference
